title: A 99% test says positive.
blocks: A rare disease affects one person in a hundred. You take a test that is ninety-nine percent accurate, and it comes back positive. What's the chance you're actually sick? Most people say ninety-nine percent.
Here's what ninety-nine percent accurate means. If you're sick, the test catches it ninety-nine times out of a hundred. If you're healthy, it wrongly says positive only one time out of a hundred.
Picture a thousand people. One percent are sick, and that's ten people. The test catches nearly all of them, so about ten true positives.
Now the healthy ones. There are nine hundred ninety of them, and one percent get a false alarm. That's about ten more positives.
So about twenty people test positive. Ten are sick, and ten are healthy. If you test positive, your chance of being sick is about fifty percent. Not ninety-nine.

The test is accurate, but the disease is rare. When something is rare, even a small error rate makes as many false alarms as real cases. That's why a positive result is a reason to test again, not to panic.
